source.title: Context-level Language Modeling by Learning Predictive Context Embeddings
source.authors: Bei-Ya Dai; Yuliang Liu; D. Xue; Yun-Chong Song; Qi-Peng Guo; Kai Chen; Xinbing Wang; Bo-Wen Zhou; Zhou-Han Lin

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and tables have minor text-extraction formatting issues, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss and downstream performance across model scales using a new context-level architecture, bearing on scaling behavior with a different modeling setup.
record.gate_note: The GPT-2 scaling comparison and its fitted parameter-count equations bear on V1 and V7. Figure 1 also plots loss against training tokens and training FLOPs, but the text supplies no numeric fitted exponents for those axes. Tables 3 and 12 report nine-task average downstream accuracy by model and shot setting. Training-curve and ablation results do not directly test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares scaling curves in a new architecture and reports different fitted perplexity exponents across architectures, bearing on V7. Its explicitly parameter-matched architecture comparisons also bear on V4. It does not establish a power law in cross-entropy loss or validate downstream predictions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ContextLM improves perplexity and average downstream performance across tested GPT-2 and Pythia scales, with better parameter, token and FLOPs efficiency. Their claims do not establish validated loss extrapolation or downstream forecasting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a new context-prediction architecture and compares its scaling behavior with GPT-2/Pythia baselines; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting protocol or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports parameter-count fit differences between GPT-2 and ContextLM-GPT2. It also varies chunk size, predictor depth, injection layer, and block size in ablations, but those results do not directly test the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: ContextLM matches baseline perplexity using 39% fewer parameters, 23% fewer tokens and 20% fewer FLOPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the architecture can improve the efficiency frontier of text pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 fits offset power laws to perplexity rather than cross-entropy loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perplexity follows an empirical offset power-law fit over the tested parameter range.

record.problems: The scaling plots do not provide extractable numeric points or uncertainty estimates. The paper gives no numeric token- or compute-axis fit exponents, and its downstream averages are descriptive rather than validated forecasts from fitted scaling laws.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the listed versions were omitted. Individual benchmark-task scores, perplexity tables outside the scaling fits, instruction-following evaluations, and ablations were not included because they do not directly measure the specified versions.

untested.parts: Power-law form in held-out cross-entropy loss, non-bottleneck conditions, and validity over several orders of magnitude. GPT-2 parameter counts span only about twelvefold; an offset power law in perplexity does not imply the same form in loss.
Small-run fits predicting substantially larger runs.
Fixed-compute allocation searches and stable parameter/token allocation exponents.
A wide sweep of depth and width at fixed total parameter count; broad architectural generality beyond the tested context-predictor comparison.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes; the fine-tuning evaluations do not fit such laws.
A quantitative or validated predictive relationship between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss. Increasing nine-task averages alone establish a trend.
Sensitivity to fitting method, parameter-count convention, schedule or data; explanations of published disagreements; compute-optimal allocation and departures from a single power law.

missing.what: Explicitly parameter-matched architecture comparisons are missing. Section 7.6 states that GPT2-PM aligns total parameter count with ContextLM. Table 11 supplies their held-out OpenWebText perplexities at four scales, allowing direct comparison of loss at fixed parameter count.

The fixed-backbone context-injection-layer sweep changes the encoder/decoder split without changing the total number of backbone layers. This architecture comparison bears on V4, although precise curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied extraction.

record.verdict_notes: No tools or external sources were used. No V1 or V6 verdict is assigned because the supplied results do not establish their defining power-law-loss and predictive components. Missing V4 results support a verdict based directly on the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports parameter-count fits and plots token- and compute-based scaling, but does not give numeric fitted exponents for tokens or FLOPs, or establish the stated non-bottleneck conditions over several orders of magnitude.
No test of predictions from fits on small runs against substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute search or fitted compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled sweep of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The experiments are text pretraining; no tests of other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling laws.
The paper reports downstream averages across model sizes and shot settings, but does not fit or validate a predictive mapping from pretraining loss or scale to downstream performance.

The GPT-2 and ContextLM parameter-count fits have different reported exponents, but the study does not vary fitting methods, parameter-count conventions, data, or training schedules to isolate their effects; it does not test compute-optimal allocation or curve bending.

rows.operation_detail: Compared perplexity across model parameter counts
rows.value: figure only; text reports ContextLM-GPT2 matches baseline perplexity with 39% fewer parameters
rows.note: The text says ContextLM-GPT2 consistently outperforms GPT-2 across the plotted scaling dimensions. The plotted numeric points are not available in the text.
rows.check: The 39% parameter saving is an efficiency comparison, not evidence that cross-entropy loss follows a power law. The figure's numeric points and uncertainty are unavailable. GPT-2 backbones range from 124M to 1.5B; ContextLM adds predictor parameters.

rows.subject: GPT-2 family and ContextLM-GPT2 family
rows.size_stated: GPT-2 family; Figure 1 shows 120M to 1.5B parameters
rows.operation_detail: Reported fitted perplexity equations as a function of parameter count
rows.note: The extraction does not preserve the superscript/sign formatting reliably. The reported exponents are 0.591 and 0.671; the two model setups have different fitted coefficients and exponents.
rows.check: These are fits to perplexity, not cross-entropy loss. The reported exponent magnitudes differ, 0.591 versus 0.671; no fit uncertainty or significance is supplied.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 parameter-matched standard-layer versus context-predictor architectures, OpenWebText evaluation
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: Table 11 gives PM versus ContextLM perplexities of 21.61/20.68, 17.87/17.03, 16.18/15.41 and 15.14/14.60, corresponding to modest cross-entropy differences of approximately 0.036–0.049 nats/token.
relationships.display_finding: Standard versus ContextLM perplexities were 21.61/20.68, 17.87/17.03, 16.18/15.41 and 15.14/14.60, corresponding to cross-entropy reductions of approximately 0.036–0.049 nats/token.

relationships.condition: Architecture-dependent fitted perplexity curves on OpenWebText
relationships.reason: r4 reports fitted exponent magnitudes of 0.591 for GPT-2 and 0.671 for ContextLM; this supports setup dependence descriptively, without uncertainty estimates or an isolated causal attribution.
relationships.display_finding: Fitted exponent magnitudes are 0.591 for GPT-2 and 0.671 for ContextLM, without uncertainty estimates or an isolated causal explanation.
